articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 fixes including a SharePoint zero-day and 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender bug, while Chrome patches its fourth zero-day this year. When AI gets better at finding vulns than humans, Patch Tuesday becomes an existential crisis.

articles.title: A “Scheme” Against Dobbs: SCOTUS Dissent Hints at Next Phase of Abortion Rights Fight
articles.summary: Another CVSS 10.0 Cisco SD-WAN bug gets exploited in the wild—that's two perfect 10s this year. Either Cisco's having the worst year ever or someone's really angry at their licensing fees.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas gets pwned, disrupting schools nationwide as hackers deface login pages with ransom demands. Nothing says 'modern education' like your LMS getting ransomed by script kiddies.

articles.title: MPs want social media treated more like unsafe toys than harmless apps
articles.summary: OpenAI catches malware via poisoned npm packages that hit two employee machines, stealing internal creds. Even the AI overlords can't escape supply chain attacks—how beautifully ironic.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram kills its barely-used E2E encryption feature after years of promising default encryption across Meta platforms. Meta breaks another privacy promise—shocking absolutely no one who's been paying attention.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Apple finally delivers E2E encrypted RCS in iOS 26.5, securing Android-iPhone chats by default. Only took them forever, but better late than letting the feds read your emoji reactions.

articles.title: The Boring Stuff is Dangerous Now
articles.summary: EFF launches offline campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid, who started editing at age 12 and became a prolific open-source blogger. Kid went from Wikipedia edits to political prisoner—the Saudi regime really hates free information.

articles.title: For ‘Survivor’ Legends Who Keep Coming Back, Outplaying and Outlasting Is a ‘Religious Experience’
articles.summary: Pwn2Own Berlin day two nets researchers $385k for 15 zero-days, pushing the total past $900k and 39 vulns. When ethical hackers are making bank faster than crypto traders, you know the software ecosystem is properly fucked.

articles.title: OpenLoop Health confirms January 2026 Data breach affecting 716,000
articles.summary: Congress demands answers from Instructure after Canvas hack hit 9,000+ schools using a single exploit. House Homeland Security finally notices EdTech security is a dumpster fire—only took a nationwide school disruption.

articles.title: Grafana GitHub Token Breach Led to Codebase Download and Extortion Attempt
articles.summary: New Linux kernel flaw 'Fragnesia' grants root access with public exploit code, following the Dirty Frag lineage. Linux privilege escalation bugs are having a moment—memory management is apparently harder than rocket science.
